title: System Design & Cloud

nodes.title: Scalability Fundamentals: Vertical vs Horizontal Scaling
nodes.subtitle: Scale-up vs scale-out, stateful vs stateless servers, latency vs throughput, bottlenecks
learning_objectives: Analyze application bottlenecks and choose between vertical and horizontal scaling strategies
Design completely stateless web application tiers capable of dynamic auto-scaling
feynman_prompts: Why is designing servers to be stateless essential before horizontal auto-scaling can function?
key_misconceptions: Storing user session data in server local memory, preventing horizontal scaling

nodes.title: Load Balancing & Traffic Distribution
nodes.subtitle: Layer 4 vs Layer 7 load balancing, round-robin, least connections, IP hash, reverse proxies, health checks
learning_objectives: Distribute incoming traffic across server fleets using Layer 7 load balancers
Configure active health checks and implement graceful connection draining during server rollouts
feynman_prompts: What is the functional difference between Layer 4 (TCP) and Layer 7 (HTTP) load balancing?
key_misconceptions: Relying on DNS round-robin alone for load balancing without health checks or failover

nodes.title: Database Scaling: Read Replicas & Connection Pooling
nodes.subtitle: Primary-replica topology, read/write splitting, replication lag, connection poolers (PgBouncer)
learning_objectives: Route read queries to read replicas while directing writes strictly to the primary database
Handle replication lag anomalies where a user writes data and reads stale replica data immediately
feynman_prompts: How does replication lag cause 'read-your-own-writes' consistency anomalies for users?
key_misconceptions: Sending all read and write queries to the primary database when 95% of traffic is read-only

nodes.title: Distributed Caching Strategies: Redis & Memcached
nodes.subtitle: Cache-Aside, Write-Through, Write-Behind, TTL, cache invalidation, cache stampede (thundering herd)
learning_objectives: Implement the Cache-Aside pattern to reduce database query load by 90%
Mitigate cache stampede (thundering herd) using probabilistic early expiration or mutex locks
feynman_prompts: What are the trade-offs between Cache-Aside and Write-Through caching patterns?
key_misconceptions: Treating distributed caches as persistent authoritative storage without backing databases

nodes.title: Content Delivery Networks (CDNs) & Edge Caching
nodes.subtitle: Edge points of presence (PoP), static vs dynamic asset caching, Cache-Control headers, stale-while-revalidate
learning_objectives: Accelerate global asset delivery and reduce origin load by configuring CDN edge caching
Implement optimal Cache-Control headers, ETags, and stale-while-revalidate directives
feynman_prompts: How do CDNs reduce network latency for geographically distributed end users?
key_misconceptions: Caching user-specific private data on public CDN edge nodes without Cache-Control: private

nodes.title: Database Sharding & Horizontal Data Partitioning
nodes.subtitle: Horizontal sharding, shard keys, range vs hash-based sharding, re-sharding challenges, cross-shard joins
learning_objectives: Select optimal shard keys that distribute data and traffic evenly without hotspots
Analyze the operational complexity and trade-offs of cross-shard joins and distributed transactions
feynman_prompts: Why does picking a monotonically increasing shard key (like timestamp) cause write hotspots?
key_misconceptions: Sharding databases prematurely before exhausting index, caching, and read-replica scaling options

nodes.title: Distributed Systems Theory: CAP & PACELC Theorems
nodes.subtitle: Consistency, Availability, Partition Tolerance, Eventual Consistency, PACELC model
learning_objectives: Evaluate distributed system trade-offs between strong consistency (CP) and high availability (AP)
Apply the PACELC theorem to analyze latency vs consistency trade-offs when no partition exists
feynman_prompts: Why does the CAP theorem state that in the presence of a network partition, a system must choose between C and A?
key_misconceptions: Assuming a distributed system can achieve 100% strong consistency and 100% availability during network splits

nodes.title: Consistent Hashing & Distributed Ring Topologies
nodes.subtitle: Hash ring, virtual nodes, rehashing overhead, distributed key distribution (DynamoDB, Cassandra)
learning_objectives: Distribute keys across a dynamically scaling cache cluster using consistent hashing rings
Mitigate hotspot imbalances on the hash ring by implementing virtual nodes (vnodes)
feynman_prompts: Why does traditional modulo hashing (hash(key) % N) fail catastrophically when a cache server is added or removed?
key_misconceptions: Using naive modulo hashing for distributed cache clusters that resize dynamically

nodes.title: Message Queues & Asynchronous Processing
nodes.subtitle: Message queues (RabbitMQ, SQS), point-to-point, task retries, exponential backoff, dead-letter queues
learning_objectives: Decouple synchronous HTTP request handling by offloading heavy work to background message queues
Handle message processing failures gracefully using exponential backoff and dead-letter queues
feynman_prompts: Why is decoupling via message queues critical for protecting backend systems against bursty traffic spikes?
key_misconceptions: Processing long-running multi-second tasks inside the user's synchronous HTTP request thread

nodes.title: Event-Driven Architecture & Streaming with Kafka
nodes.subtitle: Event streams, Apache Kafka, topics, partitions, consumer groups, offset management, event ordering
learning_objectives: Architect scalable event-driven systems using publish/subscribe event streams in Apache Kafka
Guarantee in-order event processing within specific entities using Kafka partition keys
feynman_prompts: How do Kafka consumer groups enable parallel processing of partition streams without duplicate consumption?
key_misconceptions: Assuming Kafka guarantees global ordering across all partitions instead of per-partition ordering

nodes.title: Distributed Rate Limiting & Throttling Algorithms
nodes.subtitle: Token bucket, leaky bucket, fixed window, sliding window log, sliding window counter, Redis rate limiters
learning_objectives: Protect public APIs against abuse and DDoS using Redis sliding window rate limiters
Compare the memory efficiency and burst tolerance of Token Bucket vs Sliding Window Counter
feynman_prompts: How does the Token Bucket algorithm handle sudden bursts of traffic while enforcing average rates?
key_misconceptions: Implementing naive in-memory rate limiting that fails when applications scale across multiple server instances

nodes.title: Distributed Unique ID Generation (Snowflake / UUIDv7)
nodes.subtitle: UUIDv4 random vs UUIDv7 time-ordered, Twitter Snowflake ID generation, 64-bit integer IDs
learning_objectives: Generate globally unique, time-sortable 64-bit IDs at high concurrency using Snowflake architecture
Optimize database B-Tree index locality using time-ordered UUIDv7 instead of random UUIDv4
feynman_prompts: Why does inserting random UUIDv4 primary keys cause catastrophic B-Tree index fragmentation at scale?
key_misconceptions: Relying on single centralized database auto-increment IDs in distributed multi-region databases

nodes.title: Microservices Architecture & API Gateways
nodes.subtitle: Service decomposition, API Gateways (Kong, Envoy), routing, authentication offload, service mesh
learning_objectives: Decompose monolithic architectures into bounded context microservices
Centralize cross-cutting concerns (authentication, TLS termination, rate limiting) at the API Gateway
feynman_prompts: Why should an API Gateway handle perimeter authentication rather than duplicating auth logic in every microservice?
key_misconceptions: Creating distributed monoliths where every microservice requires synchronous REST calls to 10 others

nodes.title: Distributed Transactions & The Saga Pattern
nodes.subtitle: Two-Phase Commit (2PC) limitations, Saga pattern (Choreography vs Orchestration), compensating transactions
learning_objectives: Maintain data consistency across distributed microservice databases using the Saga pattern
Design and execute idempotent compensating transactions when a distributed step fails
feynman_prompts: Why is Two-Phase Commit (2PC) an anti-pattern in modern cloud architectures due to blocking locks?
key_misconceptions: Assuming traditional ACID transactions can span across separate microservice database boundaries

nodes.title: System Resilience: Circuit Breakers & Bulkheads
nodes.subtitle: Cascading failures, Circuit Breaker pattern (Closed, Open, Half-Open), bulkheads, timeout budgets
learning_objectives: Prevent cascading system collapse using Circuit Breakers that fail fast during dependency outages
Isolate critical resource pools using the Bulkhead pattern to prevent resource exhaustion
feynman_prompts: Explain the state transitions of a Circuit Breaker: Closed -> Open -> Half-Open -> Closed.
key_misconceptions: Retrying failed dependency requests infinitely with zero delay, amplifying downstream outages (retry storm)

nodes.title: Cloud Object Storage & Media Pipelines
nodes.subtitle: Block vs file vs object storage, Amazon S3, presigned upload URLs, multipart uploads, lifecycle policies
learning_objectives: Architect scalable file upload systems using secure client-side S3 presigned URLs
Manage storage costs effectively using automated object lifecycle transitions to cold storage
feynman_prompts: Why is object storage (S3) dramatically more scalable and cost-effective than block storage for media assets?
key_misconceptions: Uploading multi-gigabyte video files directly through application server memory

nodes.title: Distributed Tracing & System Observability
nodes.subtitle: OpenTelemetry, trace IDs, span contexts, distributed trace propagation, latency heatmaps
learning_objectives: Track end-to-end user request flows across 20+ microservice boundaries using OpenTelemetry trace IDs
Diagnose distributed tail latency bottlenecks (p99 latency) using distributed spans
feynman_prompts: How do distributed trace contexts propagate across HTTP and gRPC network boundaries using W3C headers?
key_misconceptions: Relying on isolated server log files without correlation IDs when debugging distributed failures

nodes.title: Disaster Recovery & Multi-Region Cloud Architecture
nodes.subtitle: Active-Passive (Pilot Light, Warm Standby), Active-Active multi-region, DNS failover (Route 53)
learning_objectives: Architect multi-region cloud deployment topologies with automated Route 53 health-check failover
Balance the extreme cost and complexity of Active-Active systems against business RTO/RPO requirements
feynman_prompts: What are the severe distributed data conflict challenges (split-brain) inherent in multi-region Active-Active setups?
key_misconceptions: Assuming multi-region deployments are trivial without solving multi-master database write conflicts

description: Master System Design & Cloud with an industry-standard, comprehensive curriculum spanning 18 core and advanced milestones.
